trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Lost money: -17.40% total return vs +14.41% for the index, -19.20pp residual after beta, -25.8% max drawdown, 0.87% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at -17.40% - a 17,401 dollar loss on 100,000 of starting capital, in a market that returned +14.41%.
The momentum premium it is built to harvest was live (+8.30%) and the account STILL lost 17.40% - so the loss came from implementation, timing or leverage, not from a missing signal.
The liquidity premium it is built to harvest was live (-17.23%) and the account STILL lost 17.40% - so the loss came from implementation, timing or leverage, not from a missing signal.
Of the -17.40% total, about +1.80pp is explained by carrying beta 0.12 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.01); the residual -19.20pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
UNH contributed +2,740 USD across 2 closed trades; CVNA was the biggest drag at -10,117 USD.
Execution cost 865 USD (0.87% of starting capital, 3.5 bp per fill, 3.7 bp of the 2,364,071 USD traded). 80% of that was spread/depth/impact and 20% was explicit fees and rebates.
32 closed round trips, 40.6% winners, profit factor 0.38, average winner +825 vs average loser -1,481 USD, median holding 4 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 238 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 1149 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: RIVN long 2025-10-14 to 2026-02-25, -5,275 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -25.80% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-04-30, never recovered. Average gross exposure 10% of starting capital, peak leverage 1.03x.
Daily returns were -3.94 skewed with excess kurtosis +27.48; historical 95% VaR -1.18%/day with CVaR -2.83%/day. Worst single session -7.32%, best +2.30%.

Standing limitations of this simulation that apply to this participant regardless of the regime: NO REAL SHORT-INTEREST DATA offline: turnover is a proxy for a squeeze, not a measurement of one (IR-07)

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: Five-session holds through a reversal with no stop.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 70.6pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @SqueezeHunter_TF (Squeeze Hunter) ran the "liquidity squeeze" archetype. Declared thesis: When a name's daily turnover (volume / shares outstanding) spikes while price is rising, a large fraction of the float is changing hands at higher prices and short covering becomes self-reinforcing. Ride the squeeze for five sessions. Entry: Turnover today >= 2.5x its 63-session median; 3-session return > 5%; Prefer the highest turnover names, up to 3 positions. Exit: Exit after 5 sessions; Exit immediately if turnover collapses below its median. Sizing: equal 50% of equity per name = up to 150% gross. Leverage: up to 1.5x gross. Cadence: daily, horizon 5 sessions. Aggression 5/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Squeezes produce the largest single-day moves in the whole equity universe; concentration is the point.
